themes: US AI infrastructure demand is structurally outpacing Indonesian digital adoption, driving persistent alpha in US-listed tech names regardless of ID aggregate moves.
Indonesian tech remains hostage to domestic consumption and regulatory overhang, making local names tactical trades rather than core holdings.
Cross-border capital flows increasingly favor US mega-cap platforms with AI monetization, widening the valuation gap versus ASEAN tech peers.
sectors.ai: Rotate into US-listed AI infrastructure and platform names (NBIS, META, GDDY) while trimming Indonesian tech laggards; the ID underperformance is idiosyncratic, not systemic. Buy dips in CRWV and 2454 on momentum continuation, but cap exposure given normal signal. Favor US semis and cloud over local e-commerce until ID macro stabilizes.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's nickel downstreaming policy (ore export ban, HPAL smelter expansion) structurally re-rates integrated producers like NCKL and HRUM, insulating them from global price swings.
Coal remains a cash cow despite ESG headwinds, with domestic market obligation (DMO) caps and export quotas creating a stable floor for AMMN and FPNI margins through 2025.
Rupiah depreciation against USD boosts IDR-denominated earnings for miners with USD-linked offtake contracts, widening the gap versus US-listed peers and attracting foreign flows.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in nickel and coal names (NCKL, HRUM, AMMN) as Indonesia's downstream ban and smelter ramp-ups tighten supply; ALKA/BAJA spikes are speculative, take profits. Favor exporters with US-listed peers lagging, positioning for Q3 earnings beats on rupiah weakness. Trim GDST on low liquidity.

sectors.ai: Buy the US solar rebound as a read-through for Indonesia's distributed solar names, but stay selective: FSLR's 13.8% surge signals module pricing stabilization, which lifts domestic EPC margins. Rotate into US-listed yieldcos (BEP, RUN) for carry while waiting for ID policy catalysts—avoid chasing ID laggards until rupiah volatility subsides.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's middle-class expansion and urbanization continue to drive premiumization in FMCG, favoring brands with strong distribution networks like NEST and AGAR.
Digital-native consumer startups (JELI, IATA) are capturing share via e-commerce and social commerce, but their sustainability hinges on logistics cost control and repeat-purchase rates.
Regulatory shifts on food labeling and halal certification are raising compliance barriers, consolidating market share toward established players with certified supply chains.
sectors.ai: Buy JELI, IATA, and BACH on momentum, but rotate into NEST and AGAR for defensive earnings stability as US strength signals global risk-on. Trim ERTX and AYLS into rallies—their gains lack volume confirmation. Overweight staples with pricing power ahead of BI's rate hold; expect consolidation in small caps by Q3.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's logistics sector is consolidating around e-commerce last-mile delivery, favoring small-cap operators like TRUK and MITI that can scale quickly.
Government infrastructure spending on ports and toll roads is structurally lifting logistics efficiency, benefiting asset-light players like LOPI and KPIG.
Fuel subsidy reforms and digital freight matching are compressing margins for legacy players, pushing capital toward niche movers with pricing power.
sectors.ai: Buy MITI and TRUK on high-volume momentum; both show outsized gains with no fundamental news, suggesting speculative accumulation. Rotate into LOPI and KPIG for relative strength within logistics. Trim PSSI and MPXL, as their gains lag sector beta. Maintain normal exposure, but tighten stops on TAXI given its volatility.

Content localization and IP monetization (FUTR, MDIA) are becoming structural winners as Indonesian households increase discretionary spending on streaming, events, and branded experiences.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate

Government's housing subsidy recalibration and mortgage rate stability are underpinning affordable-segment demand, favoring developers with fast-turning middle-income projects over luxury inventory.

Trim if IDX property index breaks below its 20-day moving average, but hold core positions into Q3 earnings for land-sale recognition upside.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's crypto tax and Bappebti licensing regime remains a structural drag, capping local exchange volumes and forcing institutional flows offshore.
US macro easing and spot ETF inflows are the dominant global driver, transmitting volatility to IDX-listed fintech proxies rather than direct crypto exposure.
Stablecoin adoption for cross-border trade and remittance is a durable local growth vector, outpacing speculative altcoin demand in Indonesia.
sectors.ai: Buy the US-led crypto rebound selectively: BTC-linked and liquid alts (ADA, DOT, ALGO) are outperforming on risk-on flows, but Indonesia's regulatory overhang and thin local liquidity cap upside. Rotate into HELOC and ENA for yield-driven momentum, trim ZEC/HYPE on low conviction. Maintain 5-10% tactical allocation, hedge with USD stablecoins.
